chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Thal'abah ibn Maymun, from Muyassar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Two things corrupt people's prayer: a man saying 'Blessed is Your name and Exalted is Your dignity and there is no god but You,' which is merely something the Jinn said in ignorance, so God (Exalted and Majestic) narrated it from them; and a man saying 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God.'

key_terms.وَلَا إِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ: And there is no god but You

ai.seo_question: What two phrases invalidate a Muslim's prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies two specific phrases that invalidate a person's prayer if recited with the intention of worship or as part of the prayer ritual. The first is 'Blessed is Your name and Exalted is Your dignity and there is no god but You,' which is actually a phrase originally spoken by the Jinn in ignorance, later quoted by God in the Quran, but not prescribed for human prayer. The second is 'Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God,' which is incorrect because peace is for God's servants, not for the worshipper himself in this context. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on precise liturgical wording (tawqifi) and distinguishes between general greetings and specific acts of worship, ensuring that innovations (bid'ah) from pre-Islamic or non-divine sources do not corrupt the ritual.
